title: Panthers TE Mitchell Evans carted off at training camp practice
dek: Carolina Panthers second-year tight end Mitchell Evans was carted off during Tuesday's training camp practice with an ankle injury after being rolled up on during a pile. Coach Dave Canales said the initial diagnosis is not viewed as serious and the medical staff is 'pretty optimistic,' though a full evaluation is pending.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Mitchell Evans, a second-year tight end and 2025 fifth-round pick from Notre Dame, was carted off with an ankle injury during Tuesday's practice.
bottom_line: Canales' optimism suggests Evans avoids a long-term absence, but the full evaluation will determine whether he can participate in competitive camp drills during the tight-end competition. The injury's impact on Evans' role depends on the medical timeline and any limitations placed on his activities during the evaluation period.
body: Carolina Panthers second-year tight end Mitchell Evans was carted off the field during Tuesday's training camp practice with an ankle injury after being rolled up on during a pile of players.

Coach Dave Canales said the initial diagnosis indicates the injury is not viewed as serious, with the medical staff described as 'pretty optimistic.' Canales said the team will conduct a full evaluation before providing additional information.

Evans, a 2025 fifth-round draft pick from Notre Dame, recorded 19 receptions for 171 yards and two touchdowns as a rookie after being pressed into duty due to an injury to Ja'Tavion Sanders. Evans was expected to compete with Tommy Tremble and Sanders for more playing time in what the team views as an open tight-end competition.

The injury adds to a difficult week for Carolina's roster. Outside linebacker Nic Scourton, another second-year player, suffered a torn ACL, described as a season-ending injury, on the first day of training camp practice. Guard Damien Lewis worked on the side with trainers due to a calf injury, and guard Robert Hunt (back) is working his way back and expected to practice soon. Starting offensive tackles Taylor Moton and Ikem Ekwonu are absent from training camp and will miss the opener but are expected back at some point this season.
The severity and timeline of Evans' ankle injury remain under evaluation. No medical clearance or status update has been released by the team.
